messages:
Nina: SOS balcony desk update — thunderstorm forced me to move indoors. Router is now perched on a stack of design books, philodendron has declared antenna affection. Photo: https://images.redwood.example/nina-stack-router.jpg :seedling:

Rafael: Yikes. Quick check: try a channel scan and switch to a less crowded 5GHz channel if possible. Also avoid putting the router on metal surfaces.

Priya: For diagnostics run a short ping and check for packet loss. Example I ran when mine was flaky:

Priya: ```
$ ping -c 8 8.8.8.8
PING 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=1 ttl=118 time=14.2 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=2 ttl=118 time=120.6 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=3 ttl=118 time=13.5 ms
--- 8.8.8.8 ping statistics ---
8 packets transmitted, 7 packets received, 12.5% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max = 13.5/40.8/120.6 ms
```

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: observed nina-laptop intermittent losses at 176847-176848 window; 4 retransmits, avg RTT 142ms, spike at 1768480022. Suggested actions: move AP higher, enable 5GHz, or use alternate uplink.

Sam: Cheap fixes that worked for me: USB Wi-Fi dongle on a short USB extension (raise the antenna), or a $30 travel router in client mode. Powerline can be hit-or-miss depending on wiring.

Nina: Thanks! Ordered a small shelf extender and a 5GHz USB dongle. Question: Velcro straps vs zip-ties for temporary mounting — what do you use? :thinking_face:

Rafael: Velcro for rentals / easy swaps. Zip-ties if you want it rock-solid and aren't worried about holes.

Priya: If you ever see consistent high jitter, open the router UI and enable QoS for video conferencing apps as a quick mitigation.

Nina: Poll time: name the router. React with :herb: for "fern-net" or :sparkles: for "phyto-fi". GIFs encouraged.

Sam: "phyto-fi" wins on nerd points. Also post a victory pic when plant and router reach détente.

Nina: Update — shelf extender arrived, router elevated 20cm. Immediate improvement, no drops during a 30m call. Victory photo: https://images.redwood.example/nina-router-victory.jpg :tada:

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: nina-laptop events cleared at 1768480288; no retransmits observed in last 15m. Marking issue as resolved.

Nina: Thanks team! Plant and router are now coexisting peacefully. :heart:
